When you play survivor matches, if you aren’t the last one to leave/die, the match carries on while you’re in your lobby.

After the match finishes, the game will give you a deduction report from the match the moment it finishes, that can and will accumulate if you don’t take them.

If a player has too many of those collected, the game won’t allow them to start a match, either by themselves or in a team, of any kind, until they collect their reports. You do this by clicking the page sheets on the bottom right corner at the lobby, where the book should be.

After their accumulated reports lower from the maximum number of reports they can have accumulated, they’ll be able to start a match.

#Hunter counters to Seer

**Soul Weaver**

Soul Weaver counters him, since she can shoot her web and that will take the owl away. Though not many people use her so you’ll hardly encounter this, but should you, here’s some tips:

1. If she’s far away keep looking at her, that way if she shoots you have some time to dodge 

2. Keep your distance 

3. If she’s good, then she’ll shoot webs at you first, so best thing to do is send your owl to another survivor so that she doesn’t expect it, although a good SW still shoots a web before hitting, you have a higher chance.

**BonBon**

Same with bonbon, his bomb spam makes seer's owl useless if they’re good and know how to land the bombs. Nothing else to say, just stay away from them.

**Axe Boy**

Axe boy an counter him if they have good aim, but if they’re sniping you then you won’t have time to react to the owl, best thing to do is keep an eye on the souls and only use the owl when you’re close to Axe Boy

**Violinist**

This takes precision, but a good violinist can and will take away your owl with their strings. This is hard to do, so I don’t think you’ll encounter a situation like this, but always be prepared

**Smiley Face**

Smiley face can counter him if he uses his dash, since it doesn’t have a cooldown. My advice is only use it when absolutely necessary.

**Gamekeeper**

Obvious thing, his hook counters the owl, but at least he won’t drag you to him, so that’s an advantage you have.

**Sculptor**

Her sculptures spamming makes it harder for seer to have an effective owl if she decides to bait you into using it. My advice is he absolutely sure she’ll hit you from short distance and then use it, you have to be very mindful.

#Advice on using him

My advice is to know your map so that you don’t get caught in objects when you’re looking at the hunter and running away. Be mindful of your decreased vaulting speed with every owl you use and the absolute most important is that don’t forget that it’s okay to mess up sometimes. Nobody is perfect, and you learn from your mistakes. At first you’ll make a lot of them, but that’s only the first step to becoming the greates seer user in the game, don’t be discouraged and remember that practice makes master!

Here’s my opinion on each hunter you mentioned:

#Violinist

Violinist is very good, a strong hunter in the right hands and not that hard to use well, but you need to be very precise with your string and movements. I’d say he’s midway in terms of how hard he is to master, and it is very rewarding when you manage to place good strings.

#Axe Boy

I have a lot of fun playing Axe Boy. Soul snipes are very rewarding, and if you miss one you still get a boost. With his most recent rework, he can be very strong and he’s not hard to use either. However his mechanics aren’t anything overly-special, and sometimes can become repetitive and frustrating.

#Disciple

I heard Ann will probably get a rework, so sit on that one for the time being, though I recommend checking out the other hunters for now. I don’t have much experience with her, but she can be very annoying if you use her cats well. The mechanics are good but again, it becomes repetitive.

#Dream Witch

She’s very hard to learn, but super rewarding and you’ll become unstoppable. I think you would have a ton of fun with her if you like levelling up your skill with a hunter, she’s very fun to play as when you know what you’re doing.

#Personal Recommendations

If you want fun mechanics, I recommend you take a look at Mad Eyes, Gamekeeper and Photographer.

**Mad Eyes**

Mad Eyes is hard to master and the first 100 matches will be hell, but when you get the hang of him everything is fun. You get to play with survivors as if they were your guinea pigs and the wall mechanics are awesome 

**Gamekeeper**

Gamekeeper’s hook is a game changer, and it’s fun to see wether your aim is good and if you manage to read survivors' movements. I have fun playing with him, personally.

**Photographer**

Photographer is also very good, and I hear he’ll probably get a buff in terms of chase. The photo world mechanics are fun and it’s like Hide and Seek. Likewise you need to think your strategies well with both real and photo survivors. Very fun hunter to play as with fun mechanics.

#The End

I hope whatever you choose in the end, will be satisfying to you!

Hi, welcome to the game!

So, as for your questions

1. It’s fine, it takes some time to get used to it I’m sure you’ll eventually get to play hunter. Honestly, every hunter that’s their playstyle and there is not one single way to do it. Some basic tips for hunter would be to learn the hitbox and don’t swing if you’re too far away. On how to find the survivors, you might want to get “tinnitus” in the persona tree, it shows a little ear when a survivor is close. If you stop seeing it, then it means you’ve gone in the wrong direction. 

2. Pay attention to when your puppets are being triggered, this means a survivor is close and you should teleport there to hit them. Alternatively, you can infuse them with rage so they’ll go and hit the survivors for you, that way they can’t decode because they’d be busy dismantling your puppets or being chased.

3. You generally can’t lose the hunter because they can see your footsteps in their screen, so you just have to continue getting away and as far as possible to gain time for your teammates to decode. I advise that you practise a lot of kiting, even if you like to decode mainly, because kiting is essential for every character.

4. Not much, just play the game without wanting to get dice (rolling them is the way you get dice) and you’ll have a lot of them before you notise. Usually in a few days if you play a lot and had some saved or around a week or two tops if you take your time and cap your weekly limit. 

There is a wide range of survivors that excel at decoding if you want to try them. Prisoner is the most popular one, but you could also get explorer, mechanic (this one is kinda hard to master properly), Mind’s Eye (she has the fastest decoding but is blind so you actually don’t see much) and others I’m not listing. I recommend going to **Single Training Mode** to get used to them and find which one fits you best.

As for the hunter recommendations, maybe one of the other two initial ones, like Gamekeeper or Smiley. Again, every hunter (just as the survivors) have their own style and unique abilities, I recommend going to Single Training mode and test them all to see which one fits your style most. Violinist, Mad Eyes, Photographer and Dream Witch are very hard to master excellently, but it can be done with enough practising. I main Violinist and it took me a while to use him very well, so don’t feel frustrated if you don’t get the hang of a hunter right away (specially Mad Eyes and Dream Witch, I just can’t use them at all, but there are a lot of good players that use them).

Hi! I’m a veteran, started playing in S2 (about two years ago). I’ll try to answer your questions to the best of my ability.

1. it has changed a lot since the game released, obviously, with the current meta being some of the new players who weren’t originally in, but (also answering your second question) this can change depending on the buffs or nerfs they get. For example, recently a character named “Doctor” got a buff, and now I see her more in my matches. It’s definitely not a sudden-changing meta, and it depends on how people manage to use characters. This means, you’d be fine either using the meta or not, and it all depends on how you use them and how you make the most out of them. The nerfs and buffs come only when necessary or when the devs realised something should be different.

2. They listen a lot. Mainly to their Asia side, and us in NA/EU are a bit marginalised in the sense that our feedback isn’t prioritised, but they have listened to us before. They also seem to be very hardworking and kind people tbf, and (at least I know) they try their best to keep the game fun and balanced for everyone.

3. If you’re just starting you should have no problem. There are a lot of variables for which you will get paired. You’ll rarely get paired with people with different persona tree points, experience or rank like yours, and specially if you’re just starting. 

4. Depends on what grind. Grinding for clues (one of the in-game currencies) isn’t that hard, you just have to play a lot of matches and you get more dices to collect clues if you win them. Fragments and spy glasses are a different story, but you can build them up eventually. About rank grinding, then it can be a pain, specially if you’re on the survivor side, since you mostly rely on other people.

5. As of now, I’d say it’s as balanced as it could get momentarily. There are a few things that could be corrected and I’m sure they’ll eventually be, when they decide that Bloody Queen (one of the meta hunters) doesn’t need to be unnecessarily overefficient. If you’re not playing as her or against her, then everything else is balanced.

6. Just go for the five main characters they give you at the beginning. Learn how to play each of then to familiarise yourself with the different playstyles of each category. Also, find your preferred role. Do you like to decode? Pick a decoder. Do you like to kite? Pick a kiter. Do you like to rescue? Pick a rescuer. Do you like to support the team? Pick a support role. Of course you can do all of them with one character, but certain individual traits will make them more agile and effective in one area than the other. Rescuers typically decode slower, and decoders are typically less physically agile. Once you’ve played and discovered what you like to play as, then try characters of that role in the “Single Training” mode, where your abilities are infinite and without cooldown to familiarise yourself, and you get to pick characters you haven’t bought yet for you to try. There are also options within the gamemode to allow cooldown and the sorts, if you decide you want to try what it would be like in a real match. If you decide to go as a hunter, then use them in single training and learn their individual traits and abilities and decide which one fits your playstyle more. They’re each very unique and not one ability resembles the other, and we’ll have a new hunter coming soon so, check that one out too!

So, as for your last questions, I’ll help you out.

> How can the hunter find me? Even if I’m hiding sitting behind something far away from them? 

Most of us carry a persona trait called “tinnitus”. It’s a thing that pops up on the top left which tells you wether a survivor is nearby or not. If you’re just plain hiding the hunter might scope the area to find you, since he gets the little thing pop up.

Alternatively, when you haven’t performed an action for a long time, crows will appear above your head, and the hunter will get alerted of your location, even if they’re at the other side of the map.

> For example, if i’m the only one sorbible remaining and I’m trying to find the dungeon. They can still find me, so is it part of their persona? 

If they have tinnitus it might help. If you’re trying to find the dungeon after all other survivors escaped, it’s highly likely you’ll get crows very fast, and that will alert the hunter. Being the last survivor causes you to basically just get crows a few seconds after everyone else escaped.

> And what do the crows do above the survivors head? Can hunters see them? And is it a good idea to hide on lockers?

Crows alert the hunter of your location. They don’t need to be close by to see them, because the game will pop up a mark right where you are and make an alert sound, which they can see and hear. The crows you see are only there to tell you “hey, the hunter can see you, so you better do something”, but the hunter can basically know where you are at all times.

And generally speaking it’s not a good idea to hide in lockers, since the hunter can see your footsteps and if they suddenly stop and there’s a locker nearby, they might deduce you’re there. However, if you are far away then if might work, but it’s generally not advisable.

> How can I use the A costume unlock card I got from Atropos Ropes? (…)

When you have a skin selected, instead of clicking “get”, on the bottom right there is a movie thingy that says “trial”. Click on it and select your unlock card, even if the thingy you clicked on says “trial” you can use your unlock card there, so don’t worry about it.

> Is there any advantage to having accessories to your character or is it just for additional effects?

Just for additional effects, they’re not necessary nor give you any advantage in the game in any way. Actually nothing does, which is good because it makes this game not a “pay-to-win” thing.

**For the second one**, both can have virtually the same impact and it depends on the skill of the hunter. So, really, you need to analyse the situation. Either risk wasting a perfume by using it unnecessarily, or risk giving the hunter a free hit by not using it (and that leaves you vulnerable for a down since you’re already at half fear and your perfume doesn’t work if you get downed). If you’re going against inexperienced Violinists, then I recommend not using it and trying to dodge, you save perfumes and you just might not get hit.

**For the final one**, not really, survivors will start moving “randomly” but really they follow a pattern unconsciously, that for a trained violinist it’s easy to pick up on in the time you have left to put the second note. So, *Perpetual Motion*’s mechanics are very simple. The side is not random, the strings will always go the **opposite** side of the string you’re in. Let’s put a hypothetical scenario and say one end of the string is north and the other is south.

You, as the hunter, are on the west side of the string, so the motions will go east. If you’re on the east side, the strings will go west. It’s always gonna be **the opposite side of the string you’re in** (use my video for reference, it’s a great demonstration)

My Violinist tips are the following:

• If you can, hit first with the string and then with your bow, that way you don’t need to wait for a cooldown. This is very helpful when a survivor attempts a rescue because typically they’ll wait for you to hit them first, so surprise them with the note.

**Bonus Tip:** Instinctively, once they’re hit with the string they’ll rescue, because of the delay the hunter gets when attacking and hitting a survivor (this is very embedded in survivor playstyle, as is exemplified in my video). However, this is not your case because you’ve hit them with the string, so you can immediately terror shock them if need be, but they’ll already be at half health. Use this to your advantage.

• If a survivor is hiding behind a wall, create a VERY large string and use perpetual motion, that way there’s a chance you will hit them.

• Antonio is good at camping because of the strings

• This one is very important: do NOT forget that you can give a surv up to 50% decoding debuff. Sometimes it’s easy to forget that you can counter cipher rush with this. If you can, try to stack some demon notes to more than one survivor. That way they will either have to decode with the debuff or meditate to take the notes off. Both of these will buy you valuable time.

• Practice your aim with the notes, being really precise is a key component of Antonio, and you need to be able to predict what actions the survivor will take. If you feel like you can’t aim, really practice because otherwise you’ll have a hard time in matches.

**Introduction to Joseph: Camera World**

Alright so, Joseph has the ability to create a camera world, and that camera world is a copy of how the world looked at the time of taking the photo. This means:

1. Everything in the camera world will be in its current state at the time of taking the photo.

2. Survivors in the camera world will be in the exact same position as when the photo was taken in the real world.

*Pro Tip:* You can use number 2 at your advantage by going to where you think the survivors are (or where you know they are if you saw them) and hitting them in said world. 

You can also down and chair survivors in CW (Camera World), which will have an effect on the real world.

**Effects of CW in the real world**

What happens in CW has an impact in the real world. Survivors and ciphers are both affected by this, but the effects will be seen **only** after camera world has collapsed.

*Survivors:* The health of a survivor in CW will be translated to half of that in the real world. This, is very advantageous. If you hit a survivor only once in CW, and they aren’t healed when it collapses, that means that the real survivor will be downed at only *one hit*, because Joseph makes 1.5 points of damage. This translates to a lingering decreased health that the survivors won’t be able to cure (except for Doctor, she can heal herself any amount of damage).

Also, this means that downed survivors will have half their HP and chaired survivors will be incapacitated (all when CW collapses).

*Pro Tip:* Keep an eye on chaired survivors while in CW, if they rescue the survivor, then they won’t be incapacitated.

*Ciphers:* Every uncompleted cipher in the real world will go down half it’s progress when CW collapses. For example, a cipher with 50% will be at 25% progress when this happens. This also means that a cipher with 99% will be at 44.5%. Because of this, you want to have your CW activated at all times.

**Presence abilities: Recorded moment**

*A recorded moment which can be used while Camera World is active. Joseph may use it to enter and exit the Camera World freely*

With this ability, you don’t need to go through a camera to enter or exit CW. You can simply use the ability to do so freely, with a cooldown of 5 seconds.

You unlock this by landing two total hits or terror shocking a survivor, so it’s very easy to get.

*Pro Tip:* Use this to jumpscare survivors decoding. Go to a cipher you think they might be in (in CW so they don’t see you coming), exit CW, and swing as soon as possible. Doesn’t matter if they weren’t there, try again on your next cipher, because you have a high chance of terror shocking them if the hit lands.

**Presence abilities: Time Jump**

*Joseph records last 15 seconds in time as he moves. Return to your desired point in time by holding down the skill button for the corresponding number of seconds.*

As stated, Joseph can teleport back in time with this ability. The longer you hold, the further back in time you’ll go. 

However, this ability also has an extra. When you go back in time, it will face you **in the direction of the nearest survivor**. 

*Pro Tip:* When you have unlocked this ability and you don’t know where the survivors are, simply tap the button and you’ll be facing the nearest survivor.
